title: ADE comparison: eight tested, my top three

proven.label: Proven
proven.meaning: Hands-on test or definitive primary record; only the scope in the note is established.

supported.label: Supported
supported.meaning: Source or documentation supports the capability; runtime not verified.

partial.label: Partial
partial.meaning: Only part of this requirement is established.

gap.label: Gap
gap.meaning: Observed behaviour misses the requirement in the stated version and scope.

unknown.label: Unknown
unknown.meaning: Insufficient evidence for the requirement; not a failure.

personal.label: For my setup
personal.detail: Heavy dotfiles, Enterprise OpenAI and Anthropic accounts. H4 Enterprise is hard; H5 out of box is not required.

general.label: For a fresh setup
general.detail: Minimal dotfiles. H5 out of box is hard; Enterprise accounts are extra credit.

tiers.entry: Entry: what makes an app an ADE. Missing one excludes the app before ranking.
tiers.hard: Hard requirements: one miss fails the pick. Grades are never summed.
tiers.extra: Extra credit: tie-break only, never summed, never a waiver for a hard miss.

entry_terminal.label: Integrated terminal
entry_terminal.description: An integrated terminal inside the app.

entry_chat.label: Native chat
entry_chat.description: A native chat interface for agents, not only a terminal.

entry_delegation.label: Delegation
entry_delegation.description: A parent agent delegates to child agents and collects their results.

entry_keys.label: Provider keys
entry_keys.description: Bring-your-own API keys, including OpenRouter-style gateways and the major labs. A key passed through a hosted agent CLI counts; the route is recorded. Qualification requires a successful authenticated request on the tested route; an invalid-key 401 establishes transport only.

h1_tui_gui.label: H1 TUI or GUI per session
h1_tui_gui.description: Choose at launch, per pane or session, between the agent's own TUI and the app's GUI chat. Converting an existing conversation is not required.

h2_no_login.label: H2 No product login
h2_no_login.description: No separate account or sign-in for the app itself.

h3_terminal_setup.label: H3 Respects terminal setup
h3_terminal_setup.description: Respects the configured shell, startup files, env/PATH, aliases, prompt and keybindings. The shell executable and login-mode startup are separate checks. Emulator appearance is out of scope.

h4_enterprise.label: H4 Enterprise accounts (personal)
h4_enterprise.description: Works with existing Enterprise OpenAI and Anthropic accounts. Hard for my setup; extra credit for a fresh setup.

h5_out_of_box.label: H5 Out of box (general)
h5_out_of_box.description: Good defaults: a working agent without editing settings or config files. Hard for a fresh setup only.

h6_diff.label: H6 Diff and review
h6_diff.description: Integrated, syntax-highlighted diff or review of agent changes.

h7_consent.label: H7 No config changes without consent
h7_consent.description: Does not modify other tools' configs (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, shell rc) without consent. Agent-CLI trust prompts do not count against the app; a visible wizard step with a Skip button counts as consent.

x_config_files.label: Config in files
x_config_files.description: Settings live in files rather than UI-only state.

x_open_source.label: Open source
x_open_source.description: Source available under an open-source licence.

x_free_tier.label: Free tier covers core
x_free_tier.description: The core workflow is free, with no core feature behind a paywall or upsell.

x_linux.label: Linux (general)
x_linux.description: A Linux desktop build. Extra credit for a fresh setup.

x_browser.label: Integrated browser (general)
x_browser.description: A browser inside the app. Extra credit for a fresh setup.

reasons.Paseo: Best overall on the recorded tests, including a real OpenRouter request. The qualified terminal route uses a saved login-shell profile; the default remains non-login.
reasons.Sheprd: Startup and input passed with a pre-started herdr-core 0.1.18 and saved login-shell setting; native chat and child collection passed too. Open source with strong file configuration; authenticated API-key inference remains unverified.
reasons.Agentastic: Default startup forwarding and actual native key editing passed. Good defaults and free core workflow; closed source with no Linux desktop. Authenticated API-key inference remains unverified.

ranking.tie_break: Ranked recommendations use the recorded workflow, configuration and extra-credit evidence; provisional picks retain their incomplete hard-requirement grades. A recommendation is not a full qualification.
ranking.qualification_note: Paseo has authenticated gateway evidence and complete recorded hard-gate checks on its saved profile/API route. Sheprd and Agentastic now have startup/input proof but still need successful API-key inference; an invalid-key 401 is wiring evidence only.

excluded.reason: No native chat (entry). Sheprd, a Herdr-core client with chat, was tested instead.
Native chat only behind an experimental 'Agent Chat UI' flag; a flagged feature does not count (entry).
Download needs a beta access request (entry: downloadable today).
Desktop likely gated on a free account (H2); runs its own copies of the agent CLIs.
Likely needs a JetBrains account (H2); cloud features in early access.

notable_behaviour: Pane sends identified product analytics (git email as the distinct ID) on first open, before the opt-out is reachable, and writes MCP servers, skills and an AGENTS.md block into every agent's global config by default.

Orca installs status hooks into Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor and Hermes configs, on by default with no prompt. `orca agent hooks off` removes them; the status still reported enabled after removal.
Ghostex and Pane install skills into ~/.claude/skills; on this machine that path resolves into the dotfiles repo.
Orca (Yolo mode), Pane (permission prompts off, --dangerously-skip-permissions) and T3 Code (Full access) default new agents to full access.
T3 Code and OpenChamber enable usage telemetry by default, with an opt-out.
method: Paper screen of every candidate against the entry and hard tiers, from docs and source; shortlist of 8.

Hands-on test of all 8 on 12 November 2026, each in an isolated profile or data dir with the real HOME read-only where possible. Fixed prompts (for example 'Reply with exactly: PASEO_OK') with transcripts and screenshots.
Provider keys tested with a fake key; a 401 from OpenRouter itself proves the request reached the gateway. Paseo also ran a real request with a disposable key.
H7 audited by diffing other tools' config files (sha and mtime) against a 09:58 baseline.
Grades are scoped and never summed. Extras break ties only.
Continuation audit reconciled the manifest with retained tests: launch-time TUI/GUI choice counts without conversation conversion; terminal Enterprise routes count consistently.

Paseo H3 follow-up used a saved alternate login-shell profile and representative input probes through the actual app PTY. It does not establish desktop key-to-byte translation or change the default profile.

Both audiences receive three ranked recommendations. Qualified and provisional labels distinguish completed verification from incomplete hard-requirement evidence; app statuses and cell grades are unchanged by ranking.

Fresh runtime validation closed the missing Paseo child/result receipt and Sheprd/Agentastic shell-input gaps. Invalid-key 401s are retained only as transport proof; authenticated API-key requests for those two apps remain incomplete without a valid key.
note: Evidence grades are scoped, nonnumeric and never aggregated. Unknown is not failure.

runtime_validation.blocker: No valid disposable API key available; local secret-file path or environment-variable name requested.
